title: White-water rafting
summary: A full day on the Zambezi, running the rapids of the Batoka Gorge below Victoria Falls.
alt: Rafters navigating the Zambezi rapids
body: Rafting takes you below the viewpoints and into the Batoka Gorge. The Zambezi’s Grade 5 rapids make this a demanding river trip, with quieter stretches between the white water.

The route changes with river levels. Shearwater describes different high- and low-water runs; departures can change or stop when conditions are unsuitable. There is a steep walk into and out of the gorge, so the day involves more than paddling.

planning.label: Fitness
planning.text: Discuss the gorge hike and the operator’s current age and participation requirements before booking.

planning.label: Pack
planning.text: Secure footwear, swimwear, sun protection and a dry change of clothes. Leave valuables behind.

planning.label: Confirm
planning.text: Ask which route is running, what transfers and meals are included, and whether park fees are extra.

title: Helicopter flight over the Falls
summary: See the waterfall, its islands and the gorge from above on a scenic flight.
alt: A helicopter flying above Victoria Falls
highlights: Views of the river and Batoka Gorge
body: From the air, the relationship between the upper Zambezi, the waterfall and the narrow gorge becomes much easier to understand. A helicopter flight offers a different perspective from the rainforest viewpoints.

Shearwater publishes a short Flight of Angels and longer scenic options. Flight time is only part of the outing: allow for collection, check-in and the safety briefing. Routes and departures depend on conditions.

planning.label: Scheduling
planning.text: Leave flexibility in your itinerary in case weather affects the flight.

planning.label: Before booking
planning.text: Confirm the actual flight duration, passenger information requirements and seating arrangements.

planning.label: Total cost
planning.text: Ask whether transfers, park or government charges and any fuel surcharge are included.

title: Zambezi sunset cruise
summary: An unhurried evening on the upper river, with island views, birdlife and the sunset.
alt: A Shearwater cruise boat on the upper Zambezi at sunset
highlights: A gentle alternative to the adventure activities
body: Above the waterfall, the Zambezi broadens around wooded islands. A sunset cruise explores this calmer stretch of river, with opportunities to watch birds and look for hippos or crocodiles from the boat. Wildlife sightings vary.

Choose the boat as carefully as the departure time. Shared pontoon cruises and smaller vessels offer different atmospheres; menus, drinks and group sizes vary. Shearwater’s sunset offering allows around two hours on the water, with additional time for transfers.

planning.label: Choose your boat
planning.text: Ask about group size, seating, onboard facilities and the food and drinks package.

planning.label: Access
planning.text: Confirm jetty steps and boarding assistance if anyone in your group has limited mobility.

planning.label: Timing
planning.text: Check collection time and park fees. Bring a light layer for the return journey.

title: Zambezi National Park game drive
summary: Explore the woodland and river country near Victoria Falls in a guided safari vehicle.
alt: Elephants gathered beside the water
body: A game drive adds time in the bush to a Victoria Falls stay. Zambezi National Park offers the chance to look for elephant, buffalo, giraffe and antelope, with a guide helping to interpret tracks and the surrounding habitat.

Morning and afternoon departures can fit around a Falls visit. A drive is a wildlife search rather than a checklist: sightings depend on conditions and animal movements. Different reserves and routes offer different experiences, so confirm where your particular drive operates.

planning.label: Departure
planning.text: Check collection time, drive length and which park or reserve is included.

planning.label: Travelling with children
planning.text: Confirm minimum ages and whether a private vehicle would suit your group better.

planning.label: Pack
planning.text: Bring binoculars, sun protection and a layer for a cool early start. Ask about park fees.

title: Bungee jump & bridge swing
summary: Jump or swing from Victoria Falls Bridge above the Batoka Gorge.
alt: A tandem bridge swing above the gorge
duration: Allow a half day with transfers
body: Victoria Falls Bridge is the setting for the 111-metre bungee jump, as well as a bridge swing and slide. These are different activities with different sensations; choose the one you actually want rather than treating them as interchangeable.
The bridge sits between Zimbabwe and Zambia. Registration, access and the safety briefing take longer than the jump itself, and weather or operational conditions can affect the programme.

planning.label: Participation
planning.text: Confirm the selected activity’s age, weight and health requirements directly with the operator.

planning.label: Documents
planning.text: Ask what passport and bridge-access documentation you need for your departure point.

planning.label: Booking
planning.text: Check transfers, photography costs and the procedure if weather interrupts the activity.

title: Chobe day trip, Botswana
summary: Extend your stay with a cross-border wildlife day on the Chobe River and in the national park.
alt: An elephant beside an open safari vehicle in Chobe National Park
highlights: A Botswana extension from Victoria Falls
body: Chobe National Park in Botswana is known for its elephant herds and river wildlife. A day trip from Victoria Falls can combine a boat safari with a game drive, giving two perspectives on the riverfront habitat.

It is a full day with road transfers and a border crossing, rather than a quick local excursion. Programmes differ: check whether your selected trip includes both activities and where lunch fits into the day. Sightings cannot be guaranteed.

planning.label: Travel documents
planning.text: Confirm entry and re-entry requirements for your nationality and itinerary before committing.

planning.label: Programme
planning.text: Ask about collection time, border transfers, lunch, park fees and the expected return.

planning.label: Pacing
planning.text: Keep the evening free rather than pairing this outing with another fixed departure.

title: Elephant sanctuary visit
summary: Learn about the care and conservation work described by the local sanctuary operator.
alt: Visitors and a guide observing the elephants at the Wild Horizons sanctuary
highlights: Ask about elephant care and conservation
An alternative to a conventional game drive
body: Wild Horizons describes its Elephant Sanctuary and Orphanage as a refuge for elephants affected by injury, displacement and human–wildlife conflict. A visit is an opportunity to ask about individual animals and the care programme.

Sanctuary activities differ from observing free-ranging wildlife on safari. Before choosing a visit, ask what interaction takes place, how animal choice is respected and how the programme is managed. We do not treat an operator’s conservation description as independent welfare certification.

planning.label: Programme
planning.text: Confirm which visit is available, its duration and whether transport is included.

planning.label: Animal welfare
planning.text: Ask for the current interaction policy and what is optional for both visitors and animals.

planning.label: Families
planning.text: Check age limits, walking surfaces and supervision requirements.

title: Village & community visit
summary: Spend time with local hosts beyond Victoria Falls town and learn about everyday rural life.
alt: Visitors and a local host during a village visit
highlights: Context beyond the main visitor attractions
A shorter outing to combine with other plans
body: A hosted village visit offers a different perspective on the region from a sightseeing tour. Wild Horizons’ Meet the People programme visits a rural community outside Victoria Falls, introducing guests to homes, daily work and local customs.
The visit should follow the hosts’ lead. Daily life is not a fixed performance, so the activities and people you meet may change. Confirm the exact community and programme when booking.

planning.label: Respectful visiting
planning.text: Ask before taking photographs, and follow your host’s guidance about clothing and conduct.

planning.label: Community benefit
planning.text: Ask how hosts are paid and how the visit supports the community.

planning.label: Practicalities
planning.text: Confirm walking distances, transfers and whether a meal or refreshments are included.

title: Guided Victoria Falls walk
summary: Follow the Zimbabwean rainforest paths to the waterfall viewpoints with a guide.
alt: Golden light and mist above Victoria Falls
body: The Zimbabwean rainforest viewpoints bring you close to the waterfall and the spray that sustains the surrounding vegetation. A guide adds context about the river, landscape and history as you move between viewpoints.

Water volume changes through the year. Heavier flow brings more spray, while lower water can reveal more of the rock face and gorge. Neither the visibility nor the amount of water is identical from visit to visit.
bestFor: A first visit to the Falls

planning.label: What to wear
planning.text: Choose shoes with grip and bring a rain layer. Protect cameras and phones from spray.

planning.label: Access
planning.text: Discuss walking distance and step-free route options if mobility is a concern.

planning.label: Entry
planning.text: Confirm whether admission is included and which identification is needed for your entry category.

sources.title: Zambia Tourism · Water levels and visiting

title: The Boma — Dinner & Drum Show
summary: A four-course dinner and an evening of dance, singing and participatory drumming.
alt: A chef presenting dinner at The Boma in Victoria Falls
body: The Boma combines dinner with an organised entertainment programme on the Victoria Falls Safari Collection estate. The meal includes a starter, soup, a barbecue-style buffet and dessert, with local dishes among the choices.

Drumming is part of the evening, with guests invited to join in. Expect a sociable, lively venue rather than a quiet dinner for two. The food and performance are the main reasons to go; participation can be discussed with the venue.

planning.label: Dietary needs
planning.text: Tell the venue about allergies and dietary requirements in advance; confirm what can be accommodated.

planning.label: Getting there
planning.text: Check dinner arrival time and arrange the return transfer to your hotel.

planning.label: Budget
planning.text: Ask which drinks, transport and optional purchases are outside the dinner price.

sources.title: Victoria Falls Safari Collection · The Boma

title: Batoka Gorge swing
summary: A harnessed free fall and long pendulum swing into the Batoka Gorge with Wild Horizons.
body: The Wild Horizons gorge swing launches from the gorge edge rather than Victoria Falls Bridge. A harnessed drop becomes a pendulum swing above the river, offering a different experience from the bridge bungee.

The high-wire site is associated with the Lookout Café area, making a meal with a view a possible addition to the outing. Keep the activity booking and restaurant reservation separate unless your selected package includes both.
highlights: Different location from the bridge activities

planning.label: Choose the right activity
planning.text: Confirm that the booking is for the Wild Horizons gorge swing, rather than the bridge swing.

planning.label: Participation
planning.text: Ask about age, weight, health and tandem restrictions for your chosen departure.

planning.label: On the day
planning.text: Allow for registration and the safety briefing, and confirm transport and weather arrangements.

alt: A participant starting a harnessed gorge swing

title: Gorge zipline
summary: Travel across the Batoka Gorge on the Wild Horizons high-wire zipline.
duration: A short outing with briefing time
bestFor: Gorge views with an adrenaline element
body: A zipline gives you a moving view of the gorge while suspended from a cable. Wild Horizons lists it alongside the gorge swing and other high-wire activities, but the zipline is a distinct product.
Check whether you want the zipline on its own or a combination of activities. A high-wire pass can have different inclusions, restrictions and time requirements from a single ride.
highlights: A cable ride across the gorge
A separate option from the gorge swing
Can be considered alongside other high-wire activities

planning.label: Your booking
planning.text: Confirm the product name and what a combination pass actually covers.

planning.label: Participation
planning.text: Ask about the operator’s weight, age and harness requirements.

planning.label: Timing
planning.text: Check briefing, transfer and weather arrangements before adding another fixed booking.

alt: A participant travelling on a zipline

title: Livingstone Island & Devil’s Pool
summary: Visit Livingstone Island on the Zambian side, with a seasonal pool swim when conditions allow.
duration: Depends on the selected island visit
bestFor: An island visit at the edge of the Falls
body: Livingstone Island sits at the waterfall’s edge on the Zambian side. The operator offers guided island visits with different meal and departure options; a pool swim is a seasonal part of the experience, not a year-round guarantee.

Devil’s Pool and Angel’s Pool have different operating conditions. The operator can close swimming or walking without notice when river levels are unsuitable. A trip from Zimbabwe also requires planning the border crossing and the transfer to the correct meeting point.

planning.label: Water conditions
planning.text: Confirm which island and swimming programme is operating on your exact dates.

planning.label: Participation
planning.text: The published minimum ages differ for island visits and swimming; confirm current requirements and swimming ability with the operator.

planning.label: Cross-border travel
planning.text: Check Zambia entry and Zimbabwe re-entry requirements for your nationality, and arrange sufficient transfer time.

alt: A guided pool experience at the edge of Victoria Falls

title: Vulture Culture Experience
summary: A short vulture-feeding and conservation interpretation session at Victoria Falls Safari Lodge.
body: Victoria Falls Safari Lodge hosts a Vulture Culture Experience that introduces visitors to wild vultures and their conservation challenges. The session is distinct from a game drive or a captive-bird show.

The estate publishes a lunchtime programme, but check the current time, visitor access and any charge before travelling. You can also ask about booking lunch at the lodge, rather than assuming a restaurant reservation is included.
highlights: Can fit into a less crowded day

planning.label: Before setting out
planning.text: Confirm the current session time and access for non-resident visitors.

planning.label: Visitor arrangements
planning.text: Ask about any charge, group arrangements and viewing-platform access.

planning.label: Pair with lunch
planning.text: Reserve MaKuwa-Kuwa or another estate venue separately if you want a meal afterwards.

sources.title: Victoria Falls Safari Collection · Vulture Culture FAQs

alt: Wild vultures gathering during the Vulture Culture feeding programme

title: Simunye — The Spirit of Africa
summary: An evening production combining storytelling, puppetry, music and dance at Victoria Falls Theatre.
body: Simunye follows the journey of Bomani and his elephant companion Ndlovu, using puppetry, music and dance to tell a story about belonging and community. The production is presented by Victoria Falls Theatre Company.
The venue is the open-air Victoria Falls Theatre at Elephant’s Walk. This is a performance booking, separate from a dinner show: plan your meal and transport around the current performance schedule.

planning.label: Tickets
planning.text: Check performance dates, start time, seating and age guidance before booking.

planning.label: Dinner
planning.text: Allow time to eat before or after the performance; do not assume dinner is included.

planning.label: Venue
planning.text: Confirm access needs and the arrangements for weather at the open-air theatre.

alt: Performers on stage in Simunye

title: Art galleries & local crafts
summary: Make time for wildlife photography, sculpture and independent art and craft stops.
duration: An hour or an open afternoon
body: A visit to a gallery can add a quieter hour to a busy itinerary. Tami Walker’s Fine Art Gallery in town focuses on wildlife photography; other art and craft stops offer different media and perspectives.

Treat this as a self-guided idea rather than a bookable tour. Check each gallery’s current location and visiting hours. AVAC Arts’ published gallery material identifies an airport location, so do not assume every art stop is part of the same walk through town.

planning.label: Plan the route
planning.text: Check current addresses and choose nearby stops rather than assuming a single art district.

planning.label: Buying artwork
planning.text: Ask about the artist, provenance, packing and any shipping arrangements before purchasing.

planning.label: Visiting
planning.text: Confirm opening hours directly, especially before making a dedicated trip.

alt: The interior of Tami Walker Fine Art Gallery in Victoria Falls

title: Upper Zambezi canoe safari
summary: Paddle the channels and small rapids above the Falls, with riverbank wildlife and time away from town.
alt: Canoes on the Upper Zambezi at sunset
body: A canoe safari follows the upper Zambezi through the national park, well upstream of the waterfall. Guides lead the route through channels and small rapids, with opportunities to watch birds and look for animals along the banks. Sightings are never guaranteed.

Victoria Falls Canoeing Company offers a day trip with transfers, a drive to the launch site, a briefing and paddling instruction, breakfast and lunch. Raft floats and overnight camping programmes are alternatives; confirm the programme that suits your group.

planning.label: Programme
planning.text: Allow a full day for the canoe outing. Ask separately about raft floats and trips with one or more nights at camp.

planning.label: Participation
planning.text: The operator lists a minimum age of nine and reasonable fitness. Discuss swimming ability and any concerns before booking.

planning.label: Inclusions
planning.text: Confirm park fees, meals, transfers and river conditions for your date.

sources.title: Official operator · Upper Zambezi canoe safari

title: Zambezi dinner cruise
summary: Stay on the river after sunset for dinner on board, with open-water views and an unhurried evening.
alt: Guests dining on a Zambezi riverboat at sunset
highlights: Sunset followed by dinner on board
An evening alternative to a sunset-only cruise
body: A dinner cruise combines an upper Zambezi outing with a meal on board. Arrive for the changing light, watch the banks as the boat travels upstream and settle in for dinner as the evening develops.

Wild Horizons describes its Malachite dinner cruise as a roughly three-and-a-half-hour experience. Boats and meal arrangements differ between operators, so compare the actual vessel, menu and inclusions rather than choosing on the cruise name alone. Wildlife sightings depend on the day.

planning.label: Dining
planning.text: Share dietary requirements when enquiring and confirm the menu and drinks included.

planning.label: Timing
planning.text: Check pickup and return times before combining this with another evening activity.

planning.label: Access
planning.text: Ask about boarding steps, seating and any mobility needs. Confirm river fees and hotel transfers.

title: Lunar rainbow tour
summary: Visit the Falls around the full moon for the chance to see a rainbow formed by moonlight in the spray.
alt: A moonlit rainbow in the mist above Victoria Falls
highlights: Guided nighttime visit to the Falls
Selected dates around the full moon
A different perspective on the rainforest viewpoints
body: Moonlight meeting the waterfall spray can produce a lunar rainbow, or moonbow. A guided evening visit offers a chance to see this quieter nighttime view of Victoria Falls.

This outing runs on selected dates around the full moon. Visibility depends on the moon, mist and weather, so a moonbow cannot be promised. Check the viewing dates before setting your itinerary and ask about the current evening access arrangements.

planning.label: Dates
planning.text: Confirm the operator’s viewing calendar and whether a tour is running during your stay.

planning.label: Conditions
planning.text: Expect potentially wet paths and limited light. Wear shoes with grip and follow your guide.

planning.label: Photography
planning.text: Ask about camera equipment and the time available at viewpoints; confirm transfers and entry fees.

title: Victoria Falls canopy tour
summary: Follow a guided course of cable slides, trails and a rope bridge through the forest above the gorge.
alt: A harnessed visitor travelling along the Victoria Falls canopy course
highlights: A sequence of nine cable slides
body: The canopy tour links a series of slides with forest trails and a rope bridge in the Zambezi gorge woodland. It is a guided course with several stages, rather than the single long crossing of the gorge zipline.

Wild Horizons describes nine slides and a cable bridge, with a safety briefing before the course begins. Allow around two to two-and-a-half hours for the activity, plus collection and return. There is walking between sections, and participants need to be comfortable moving at height.

planning.label: Suitability
planning.text: Confirm current harness, age and participation requirements for everyone in your group.

planning.label: Wear
planning.text: Choose secure walking shoes and comfortable clothes; tie back long hair.

planning.label: Inclusions
planning.text: Check transfers from your hotel and whether photographs, video or additional fees are separate.

sources.title: Official operator · Victoria Falls canopy tour

title: Batoka Gorge jet boat adventure
summary: Head into the gorge for a guided jet boat ride through the river below the Falls, with a steep hike each way.
alt: Passengers wearing helmets and life jackets on a jet boat in Batoka Gorge
body: The jet boat trip takes you down into Batoka Gorge for a powered ride on the Zambezi below Victoria Falls. Shearwater’s programme includes a steep descent to the river and a climb back out, making this a physically demanding outing as well as a boat ride.

The time on the water is around 35–45 minutes, within a longer outing that includes access and transfers. Departures depend on water levels, with closures possible at both high and very low water. Confirm the route and operating status for your date.

planning.label: Fitness
planning.text: Discuss the steep gorge hike and the operator’s health and mobility restrictions before reserving.

planning.label: Participation
planning.text: Shearwater lists a minimum age of ten, with a suitable life-jacket fit required. Confirm requirements for your group.

planning.label: Pack
planning.text: Wear secure footwear and clothes that can get wet; check park fees and transfer inclusions.

sources.title: Official operator · Batoka Gorge jet boat adventure

title: Flying Fox gorge flight
summary: Glide above Batoka Gorge in a face-down harness, taking in the river and cliffs from the air.
alt: A visitor suspended face down in a Flying Fox harness above the gorge
highlights: A different ride from the zipline or swing
body: The Flying Fox carries you across the gorge in a horizontal, face-down harness. Unlike the free fall of a gorge swing or the seated position of a zipline, the position gives a feeling of gliding over the river.

Wild Horizons describes a gentler-paced high-wire ride with views of the basalt cliffs and rapids below. The flight is one part of the outing: allow time for transfers, harness fitting and the briefing, and confirm how long the full visit will take.

planning.label: Participation
planning.text: Confirm harness fit, current weight limits and requirements for children before booking.

planning.label: Wear
planning.text: Choose secure shoes, tie back long hair and leave loose valuables at your hotel.

planning.label: Inclusions
planning.text: Check collection times, park fees, and whether photographs or video are extra.

sources.title: Official operator · Flying Fox gorge flight

title: Guided Victoria Falls bicycle tour
summary: Explore town and its surroundings with a guide, with routes that can take in the river, viewpoints and local landmarks.
alt: A group with bicycles beneath trees in Victoria Falls
body: A guided bicycle outing connects Victoria Falls town with nearby landmarks at a slower pace than a vehicle tour. Wild Horizons describes route possibilities including the upper river, Big Tree, gorge views and the bridge.

Routes and stops should be confirmed for your departure. The operator recommends basic cycling experience and lists an outing of approximately two hours. Ask about distance, terrain and the pace before choosing this for children or riders with different levels of confidence.

planning.label: Route
planning.text: Confirm the planned stops and whether bridge access is included; ask whether you need your passport.

planning.label: Equipment
planning.text: Check bicycle sizes and the current minimum age. The operator lists bicycles and helmets among the inclusions.

planning.label: Timing
planning.text: An early departure may suit warmer days. Confirm water and pickup arrangements.

sources.title: Official operator · Guided Victoria Falls bicycle tour

title: Chinotimba township tour
summary: Explore Chinotimba with a local guide, visiting neighbourhood streets and markets beyond the town’s visitor centre.
alt: Market stalls and residents in Chinotimba township
highlights: Time to learn about the town beyond the Falls
body: Chinotimba is a residential part of Victoria Falls, with its own markets, businesses and community spaces. A guided visit offers context for everyday life in the town and time to learn from someone who knows the neighbourhood.

Wild Horizons lists an approximately two-hour outing with local transfers. Stops vary with the day and the host arrangements. Treat it as a visit to a living neighbourhood: ask before taking photographs and follow your guide’s advice about entering homes or community spaces.

planning.label: Programme
planning.text: Confirm which stops are planned and the amount of walking involved.

planning.label: Visits
planning.text: Community spaces are visited only by arrangement; access to schools or other institutions is not guaranteed.

planning.label: Practicalities
planning.text: Wear comfortable walking shoes and bring sun protection. Confirm hotel pickup and return times.

title: Hosted lunch & village visit
summary: Share a home-cooked lunch with a local host, then continue with a guided visit to a rural community.
alt: A visitor and local host during a village visit near Victoria Falls
highlights: A meal hosted in a local home
body: Wild Horizons’ Cultural Connection programme pairs a home-hosted lunch with a Meet the People village visit. It brings a meal and conversation together with a guided introduction to rural life around Victoria Falls.

This is the combined option for visitors who would like more time than the standalone village visit. Confirm the host arrangements, the day’s schedule and group requirements before booking. Menus reflect the host’s cooking; share dietary needs in advance rather than assuming every request can be accommodated.

planning.label: Schedule
planning.text: Ask for the actual pickup, meal and return times; allow space in your itinerary for the combined programme.

planning.label: Group size
planning.text: The operator lists a minimum of four guests. Ask whether your party can join a scheduled departure.

planning.label: Hosting
planning.text: Confirm dietary needs, transfers and what is included. Ask your host before taking photographs.

sources.title: Official operator · Hosted lunch & village visit

title: Historic Victoria Falls Bridge tour
summary: Discover the bridge’s construction story and join a guided walk on the catwalks beneath its deck.
alt: A guide leading visitors along a catwalk beneath Victoria Falls Bridge
highlights: Views of the gorge and bridge structure
body: The historic bridge tour explores how the Victoria Falls Bridge was designed and built, with a presentation followed by guided access to catwalks beneath the deck. It offers a closer look at the steel structure and the gorge below.

This is a history tour with a walk at height, separate from the bungee, swing and bridge slide. Carry your passport for bridge-area access and confirm the current formalities. Ask whether the catwalk section suits everyone in your party before booking.

planning.label: Access
planning.text: Bring your passport and confirm bridge access requirements for your circumstances.

planning.label: Suitability
planning.text: The catwalk section involves heights. Confirm age restrictions, harness requirements and mobility considerations.

planning.label: Timing
planning.text: Allow for the presentation, walk and transfers. Check whether hotel collection is included in your quotation.

sources.title: Official operator · Historic Victoria Falls Bridge tour
